### Observed differences

- In the later window, two previously unobserved activities — A27 and A28 — each take part in about 55 in 100 cases (109 of 200 traces, versus 0 of 200 before), and they always appear together in the same traces: in about 21 in 100 cases A27 comes first, in about 34 in 100 cases A28 comes first. [OCC004, OCC005, REL009]
- A22, which previously appeared exactly once in every case (200 of 200 traces), now appears in only about 45 in 100 cases (91 of 200) and never co-occurs with A27 or A28. [OCC003, REL005, REL006]
- Routing out of A21 changed: before, all of A21's outgoing transitions went to A22; in the later window about 45% go to A22, about 34% to A28 and about 21% to A27. [DIR001]
- The new activities sit between A21 and A23: about 61% of A27's outgoing transitions lead to A23 and about 39% to A28, while about 61% of A28's lead to A27 and about 39% to A23; A27 precedes A23, and A28 precedes A23, in about 55 in 100 cases each. [DIR002, DIR003, REL007, REL008]
- A23 still occurs in every case, but in about 55 in 100 cases it now occurs without A22, and its distance from A21 shifts from always 2 positions to 2 positions (about 45 in 100 cases) or 3 positions (about 55 in 100 cases). [REL004, LAG001]
- Participation in A18 fell from about 59 in 100 to about 40 in 100 cases, while A19 rose from about 41 to about 60 in 100; neither activity repeats within a case. [OCC001, OCC002]
- The new activities occur around the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.48), and A21's mean relative position shifted slightly earlier, from about 0.46 to about 0.44; these are event positions, not clock times. [POS001, POS002, POS003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, roughly half of the executions run a new segment between A21 and A23 in which the pair A27 and A28 (in either order) takes the place of A22: about 21 in 100 cases follow A21→A27→A28→A23, about 34 in 100 follow A21→A28→A27→A23, and the remaining about 45 in 100 keep the original A21→A22→A23 path. The support is direct and relational rather than merely a frequency shift: A21's successors redistributed from A22 alone to A22, A27 and A28; both new activities precede A23; A22 and the new pair are strictly mutually exclusive; and the A21→A23 distance moves from always 2 positions to 2 or 3, exactly what a two-activity replacement implies. The 19 flagged items far exceed the roughly 0.32 expected by chance at these thresholds, and the key items rest on large samples (109 versus 0 traces for the new activities). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, LAG001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]

The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a difference in the mix of existing variants between the two finite samples (200 traces each) rather than a structural modification, since variant frequencies can differ between windows without any change — although a behaviour present in about 55% of after-window traces being entirely absent from 200 before-window traces is hard to attribute to sampling alone. The participation shift between A18 and A19 (about 59/41 to about 40/60) is a further behavioural change, but no relational or positional evidence links it to the A21–A23 segment, so its structural relationship to the rest remains open. [OCC001, OCC002]
